delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} services from the collector? Their instances, resources, alerts, tags, compliance attachments, actions and status history go with them. The agents recreate a service at their next push if it still exists. This cannot be undone.

delete.question_one: Delete this alert from the collector? The check that raised it raises it again at its next run if the cause remains. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} alerts from the collector? The checks that raised them raise them again at their next run if the cause remains. This cannot be undone.

detail.title: Application code
detail.teamsHint: Changing the teams of an app requires the AppManager privilege and the responsibility of the app; unless you are a Manager, you can only add teams you are a member of. The responsible teams manage the app, the teams it is published to see its nodes and services.
detail.editHint: The code, description, domain and ops team are changed by an AppManager responsible for the app. Renaming the code renames it on the nodes and services of the app. The ops team is an organizational group.

delete.question: Delete the {{app}} code? Its responsibles and publications go with it. This cannot be undone.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this application code? Its responsibles and publications go with it. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} application codes? Their responsibles and publications go with them. This cannot be undone.

delete.question: Delete the record for {{addr}} on {{nodename}}? If the node still reports this address, it comes back on the next asset push.

create.title: New network
create.intro: Declare an IPv4 network. The Networks view lists node addresses, not declared networks: node addresses inside the range will show its name, gateway and range in the Network column.
create.noRow: The network was created but not returned.
create.hostBits: This address has host bits set; the network address is {{network}}.
create.gatewayOutside: This gateway is outside the network.

segment.title: New network segment
segment.intro: Declare an address range of a network. Members of the segment's responsible groups may allocate its addresses; your primary group becomes responsible for it. The range must lie inside the network and must not overlap another of its segments.
segment.noNetwork: No network is declared yet: declare one with New network first.
segment.noRow: The segment was created but not returned.

typeHints.dynamic: Addresses are handed out by provisioning.

problems.before: The last address comes before the first.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this IP address? The agent of a node reports it again at its next asset push if the node still has it. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} IP addresses? The agent of a node reports them again at its next asset push if the node still has them. This cannot be undone.

detail.title: Group
detail.editHint: The name, description and privilege flag are changed here; only a Manager makes a group a privilege group or changes one. The Everybody group cannot be changed.

create.title: New group
create.intro: A privilege group grants a right across the collector. An ordinary group only gathers users, to hold responsibilities.
create.exists: A group named {{role}} already exists. Creating it again would modify it.

delete.question: Delete the group {{role}}? Its memberships, responsibilities and publications go with it. This cannot be undone.

members.title: Members
members.none: No user is member of this group.
members.hint: Memberships are changed from the panel of each user.
members.editHint: Each change is written at once. A GroupManager who is not a Manager is offered the users sharing one of their organizational groups.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this group? Its memberships go with it, as do the responsibilities and publications it gives on applications, forms, rulesets and modulesets. The Everybody group cannot be deleted. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} groups? Their memberships go with them, as do the responsibilities and publications they give on applications, forms, rulesets and modulesets. The Everybody group cannot be deleted. This cannot be undone.

menu.title: Menu entries
menu.intro: The entries the members of {{role}} see in their menu. An entry is hidden to a user only when every team of the user hides it; the Everybody group and the privilege groups do not count, the personal group of a user does.
menu.noMembers: The group has no member: the entry is hidden to nobody.
menu.hiddenForNone: Hidden to none of the members: each has another team, or their personal group, that shows it.
menu.hidePersonal_one: Also hide it on 1 personal group
menu.hidePersonal_other: Also hide it on {{count}} personal groups
menu.hidePersonalHint: For the members whose personal group alone keeps it shown; those kept by another team still see it.

detail.title: Tag
detail.editHint: The exclusion pattern is a regular expression of the tag names a node or service carrying this tag cannot carry as well; empty, it excludes nothing. Renaming a form-based tag (<form>::<name>) changes the form describing its data.
detail.deleteQuestion: Delete the tag {{name}}? Its attachments to nodes and services go with it. This cannot be undone.

create.title: New tag
create.intro: A tag marks nodes and services, to group them in filters and views. Only its name is required.
create.excludeHint: Regular expression of the tag names that cannot be attached along with this one. Optional.
create.excludeInvalid: This is not a valid regular expression.
create.dataHint: Free data attached to the tag: JSON, or plain text. Optional.

formHelp.summary: How to describe a tag's data with a form
formHelp.naming: Name the tag after a form, then two colons, then a name of your own:
formHelp.example: For instance, with the form keyval:
formHelp.tagData: The tag's own data is shared by every node and service carrying the tag. It changes in the tag's panel, by a TagManager.
formHelp.attachData: Each node or service carrying the tag has data of its own as well. It is filled in when the tag is attached, from the node or service panel, by whoever may change its tags.
formHelp.after: Pick a form to start the name with it:
formHelp.pick: Start the name with a form
formHelp.plainHint: To describe the tag's data with a form, name it <form>::<name>.
formHelp.formBased: ✓ Form-based tag: its data is described by the form {{form}}.
formHelp.missing: No form named {{form}}: the tag's data would be free JSON. Check the name before the "::".
formHelp.dataHint: Shared by every node and service carrying the tag. Optional: write it here in JSON, or after creating the tag, in its panel, through the form {{form}}.
formHelp.namingThen: The tag's data is then laid out and filled in with that form, rather than written in JSON.

create.dataAsText: Not JSON: it will be stored as plain text.

data.title: Data
data.noForm: No form named {{form}} can be read: the data is edited as text.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this tag? Its attachments to nodes and services go with it. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} tags? Their attachments to nodes and services go with them. This cannot be undone.

delete.label: Delete the user
delete.question: Delete the user {{email}}?
delete.consequence: Their team memberships, private team, identity provider links, session filter and preferences go with the account; the audit log and the history of their actions stay. They can no longer sign in. This cannot be undone.

detail.title: User
detail.editHint: A user may change their own name and email; changing another user's requires the UserManager privilege. The email is the sign-in name.

memberships.hint: Changing the groups of a user requires the GroupManager privilege; unless you are a Manager, you can only add groups you are a member of.

create.title: New user
create.intro: The collector also creates the user's private group. Only the email is required.
create.noPassword: Without a password the account exists but cannot sign in.
create.passwordsDisabled: Password sign-in is disabled on this collector: the user signs in through the identity provider.

groups.title: Groups and privileges
groups.hint: Your organizational groups decide which nodes, services and applications you see; your privilege groups decide what you may change. A GroupManager changes them from the Users view; when you sign in through your identity provider, some may follow its claims.
groups.manager: Manager grants every privilege: the other privilege groups add nothing to it.

palette.title: Theme
palette.hint: High contrast uses black or white text, visible borders and saturated colours. Colour-blind friendly shows the states in blue, gold and crimson rather than green and red. Both apply in light as in dark mode.

theme.title: Light or dark
theme.hint: Saved with your account, and applied wherever you sign in.

viewPrefs.title: Saved view settings
viewPrefs.hint: The columns, sort order, filters and page size you chose in each list follow your account.
viewPrefs.reset: Forget saved columns, sorting, filters and page sizes
viewPrefs.question: Forget the columns, sort order, filters and page size saved for every view?
viewPrefs.done: Saved columns, sorting, filters and page sizes forgotten. Every list is back to its defaults.
viewPrefs.none: No view has saved columns, sort order, filters or page size.

password.managedByProvider: Your password is managed by your identity provider: change it there.
password.title: Password
password.hint_one: At least {{count}} character. Signs you in to this interface and to the historical collector.
password.hint_other: At least {{count}} characters. Signs you in to this interface and to the historical collector.
password.same: The new password must differ from the current one.
password.done: Password changed. You stay signed in with the new one.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.hint: How the interface looks, saved with your account and applied wherever you sign in.

saved.title: Saved settings
saved.hint: What your account remembers of the lists.

identity.hint: Your name and email are yours to change; the other properties are managed by an administrator.
identity.editHint: Hover a field to change it. The email is also your sign-in name: you sign in with the new one from now on.
identity.managedHint: Your name and email come from your identity provider: change them there. The collector takes them again at each sign-in.

panelSide.title: Detail panels
panelSide.hint: The edge of the window the detail panels and their history open against. The button in the header of a panel switches it too.

language.title: Language
language.hint: System follows the language of the browser. A chosen language follows the account, on every browser.

instances.title: Service Instances

delete.label: Delete from the collector
delete.question_one: Delete this instance from the collector? Its resources, alerts and checks go with it, and every container of the service on that node. The agent recreates it at its next push if it still exists. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} instances from the collector? Their resources, alerts and checks go with them, and every container of the service on each node. An agent recreates an instance at its next push if it still exists. This cannot be undone.

instances.actionErrors_one: {{count}} unacknowledged action error in the last day
instances.actionErrors_other: {{count}} unacknowledged action errors in the last day

obsolescence.title: Obsolescence
obsolescence.intro: Warning and alert dates for each hardware model and OS release reported by nodes. The collector applies them to the matching nodes and raises dashboard alerts when they are reached.

refresh.done: Settings are up to date with the inventory.
refresh.hint: Creates a setting for every hardware model and OS release reported by nodes that has none yet. Existing settings and their dates are left unchanged.

detail.title: Obsolescence setting
detail.editHint: Only the deadlines can be changed; clearing one removes it. A change applies to the matching nodes and updates their obsolescence alerts on the dashboard.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this obsolescence setting? The next refresh creates it again, without dates, for the hardware models and OS versions the nodes still report. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} obsolescence settings? The next refresh creates them again, without dates, for the hardware models and OS versions the nodes still report. This cannot be undone.

charts.title: Charts
charts.intro: Time series of historized metrics, each defined in YAML, which reports show. A Manager sees every chart; the others see the charts published to one of their teams.

form.title: New chart
form.intro: The chart is published to your primary team, which is also made responsible for it. Creating a chart requires the ReportsManager privilege.
form.yamlPlaceholder:
Metrics:
  - metric_id: 186
    label: Nodes by OS
Options:
  stack: true
form.yamlHint: Optional: the definition can be written later. It must be valid YAML: the historized metrics drawn (metric_id) and the Options.

reports.title: Report definitions
reports.intro: Pages of charts and metrics, each defined in YAML. A Manager sees every report; the others see the reports published to one of their teams. They are read in Statistics › Reports.

preview.noHistory: No history yet: the collector records the metrics once a day.
preview.notice: Preview of the report: each metric is run now. Its placeholders stand for the nodes and services you can see, narrowed by your session filter.
preview.empty: The report has no definition yet: write one to preview it.

form.title: New report
form.intro: The report is published to your primary team, which is also made responsible for it. Creating a report requires the ReportsManager privilege.
form.yamlHint: Optional: the definition can be written later. It must be valid YAML.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.intro: SQL requests whose results feed the charts and the reports. A historized metric is computed every day and its values kept over time.

form.createIntro: The metric is published to your primary team, so that its members see it. Creating a metric requires the Manager privilege.
form.editIntro: Charts and reports using the metric read it with the new definition. Editing requires the Manager privilege.
form.sqlPlaceholder: SELECT os_name, COUNT(*) FROM nodes WHERE node_id IN (%%fset_node_ids%%) GROUP BY os_name
form.sqlHint: %%fset_node_ids%% and %%fset_svc_ids%% stand for the nodes and services of the filterset of the session where the metric is read.
form.indexHint: Columns of the result, counted from 0. Leave the instance column empty when the request returns a single value.
form.historizeHint: The collector computes the metric every day and keeps its values for the charts.

filters.title: Filters
filters.intro: A filter is one condition on a column of a collector table. Filtersets combine filters to select nodes and services.

form.createIntro: The collector checks that the column exists in the table and that no filter has the same definition.
form.editIntro: Filtersets using this filter will select according to the new definition.
form.valueHint: With LIKE, % matches any text. With IN, separate values with commas.

delete.question: Delete the filter {{label}}? This cannot be undone.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this filter? It is removed from the filtersets using it, which then select other objects. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} filters? They are removed from the filtersets using them, which then select other objects. This cannot be undone.

filtersets.title: Filtersets
filtersets.intro: A filterset combines filters, and other filtersets, with logical operators. Views and compliance rulesets use filtersets to select nodes and services.

create.title: New filterset
create.intro: Create the filterset, then add its filters in the detail panel.
create.exists: A filterset named {{name}} already exists. Creating it again would modify it.
create.statsHint: A stats filterset restricts the statistics views.

detail.title: Filterset
detail.editHint: The name and the stats type can be changed. Renaming keeps the composition and its uses.

composition.title: Composition
composition.intro: Entries are evaluated in order, each joined to the previous ones by its operator.
composition.empty: No filter yet: the filterset selects nothing.

objects.firstOnly: The first {{count}} by name. Type a name to narrow the list.

usage.title: Used by
usage.none: Not used by any filterset, ruleset or check threshold.

delete.question: Delete the filterset {{name}}? Its composition goes with it. This cannot be undone.

newFilter.title: New filter
newFilter.existing: This filter exists already: it will be reused.
newFilter.noId: The collector did not return the id of the new filter.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this filterset? Its uses go with it: the filtersets nesting it, the rulesets it restricts, the session filters, check thresholds, comparisons and sysreport grants using it. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} filtersets? Their uses go with them: the filtersets nesting them, the rulesets they restrict, the session filters, check thresholds, comparisons and sysreport grants using them. This cannot be undone.

san.title: SAN connections
san.error: Could not load the SAN connections: {{message}}
san.empty: No SAN connection known for this node: none of its adapters is plugged in a switch the collector inventories.
san.label: SAN connections of {{name}}
san.openSwitch: Show the ports of {{name}} in the SAN Switches view

attach.noCandidate: No other tag can be attached.

detail.title: Queued action
detail.missing: This action is no longer in the queue.

display.showForm: Show the value laid out by its form

forms.title: Forms
forms.intro: A form describes, in YAML, the inputs a submission expects and the outputs it runs: database insert, API call, script, mail or workflow step. The list shows the forms published to one of your groups; creating and changing them requires the FormsManager privilege.

form.createIntro: The form is published to your default group, which is also made responsible for it.
form.editIntro: Each new definition is recorded in the form's revision history.
form.yamlHint: YAML, indented with spaces. The collector refuses a definition that does not parse.

delete.question: Delete the form {{name}}, with its publications and responsibles?

preview.notice: Preview of the form as its users see it. Fill it to try its conditions and checks: submitting shows the data it would send, without running its outputs.
preview.unparsable: The definition does not parse: fix its YAML to preview the form.
preview.noOutput: The definition has no Outputs: its users could not submit it.

render.candidatesWaiting: Fill the inputs this list depends on.

delete.label: Delete
delete.question_one: Delete this form? Its publications and responsibles go with it. This cannot be undone.
delete.question_other: Delete these {{count}} forms? Their publications and responsibles go with them. This cannot be undone.

requests.title: New request
requests.intro: Choose the form of your request: browse the folders on the left, or search the whole catalog. Star the forms you use often.
requests.notFound: This form does not exist, or is not published to you.
requests.unusable: This form has no usable definition.
requests.empty: No form is available to you.
requests.noFavorites: No favorite yet: star a form to find it here.
requests.noRecent: No form submitted yet from this account.
requests.folderNotFound: This folder holds no form available to you.

payload.hint: The body sent on submission, as the inputs stand. An input whose condition does not hold is left out; an empty one is sent empty.

switches.title: SAN Switches
switches.intro: One row per switch port, with what is plugged on its other end: a node, a storage array or another switch.

allRequests.title: All requests
allRequests.intro: The requests you or your teams take part in (created, are assigned, or handled one of their steps), all of them for a Manager: their status, their steps and who they await.

teamRequests.title: Assigned to my team
teamRequests.intro: The pending requests waiting for action from my team: those whose last step is assigned to me or to one of my groups.

tiersRequests.title: Pending tiers action
tiersRequests.intro: The pending requests started by my team and waiting for action from a tier: created by me or one of my groups, and assigned to someone else.

claimMappings.title: Claim mappings
claimMappings.intro: Rules translating the claims your identity provider sends at sign-in into access to the collector and teams. A rule matches when the claim equals the value, or, for a list such as groups, contains it. Once a rule allows signing in, only the identities matching one may sign in through the provider, and those may have their account created at their first sign-in. The teams a rule names follow the claims at every sign-in; the others are managed in Teams. Signing in with a collector password is not affected.

current.title: Claims of your current sign-in
current.intro: What your identity provider sent when you signed in. Click a value to start a rule from it.
current.notOidc: You signed in with a collector password: there are no claims to show. Sign in through the identity provider to see the claims it sends.
current.none: Your sign-in carries no claim a rule could use.

form.intro: The rule applies at the next sign-in of each account, and at once to the Bearer tokens of scripts.
form.claimHint: The claim name as the provider sends it (groups, email, roles…), or a dotted path into a nested claim (realm_access.roles).
form.valueHint: Compared exactly, case included. For a list, the rule matches when the list contains this value.
form.accessHint: Once at least one rule allows signing in, the identities matching none are refused, even with an existing account.
form.teamHint: As many groups as needed. Everybody and the private groups of the users cannot be granted.
form.noEffect: Choose at least one effect: allow signing in, or grant teams.
form.teamWarning_one: {{teams}} will follow the claims: at their next sign-in through the provider, the accounts matching no rule granting it leave it, even if they were added by hand.
form.teamWarning_other: {{teams}} will follow the claims: at their next sign-in through the provider, the accounts matching no rule granting one of them leave it, even if they were added by hand.

fieldConstraints.title: Field values
fieldConstraints.intro: The attributes of nodes, services and apps whose values are constrained; the others are free text. Suggest: the detail panel offers the values of a list in a dropdown, another value can still be typed. Strict: only the values of the list. Regex: only the values matching a pattern. In strict and regex modes the collector refuses the other values a user sets, except clearing the attribute or keeping the value it holds. The values the agents report are never refused, and the values the objects hold are never changed.
fieldConstraints.loadError: Could not load the field values: {{message}}
fieldConstraints.none: No attribute is constrained: every attribute is free text.

safe.intro: The files of the collector safe you may see: those you uploaded or that are published to one of your groups, all of them for a Manager. Service configurations and compliance rulesets reference them as safe://<id>, and the agents download them with their node credentials. Each version is a row; files are encrypted at rest when the collector is configured to.

checkDefaults.title: Check defaults
checkDefaults.intro: The thresholds of a check type. A check takes, among the defaults of its type whose instance pattern matches its instance, the one of the highest priority, then of the longest pattern, unless thresholds set on it or contextual ones apply.
